title: Increase httpx timeout to prevent requests from erroring out
body: I'm developing a queued Gradio RAG-QA chatbot that streams responses. When I upload one Wikipedia page and create a FAISS vector index, the backend completes successfully in about 3.96 seconds, but the Gradio front end displays an Error instead of the upload status in the Textbox. I need demo.queue() because the chatbot streams its response. This occurs with gradio 3.27.0, gradio_client 0.3.0, langchain 0.0.228, and wikipedia 1.4.0.

symptoms_visible: The backend successfully creates the Wikipedia FAISS index in about 3.96 seconds, but the queued Gradio front end displays an Error instead of the success status in my Textbox.
N0.label: N0 queued request front-end error reported

symptoms_visible: I get the same front-end Error when testing with Gradio 3.40.1.
N1.label: N1 latest-version test unchanged

symptoms_visible: In my self-contained queued chatbot example, the front end displays Error when the generator waits five seconds before streaming; removing that wait makes it work.
N2.label: N2 five-second boundary reproduced

symptoms_visible: The same delayed queued request produces the front-end Error on my local machine, my teammate's machine, and a VM.
N2_x.label: N2_x local-environment dismissal rejected

symptoms_visible: After increasing the httpx default timeout to 30 seconds, the delayed queued request works and the Gradio front end no longer displays the timeout Error.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved with increased httpx timeout

question_patterns: Can you test the same application with the latest Gradio version and report what happens?
Does upgrading Gradio change the front-end error?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried the latest Gradio version, 3.40.1, and I get the same issue.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: After upgrading to the latest Gradio version, the request completes and the front end displays the result normally.
I tested with Gradio 3.40.0 rather than 3.40.1 and still get the same Error.

edges.comment: Reporter c3, answering the maintainer's c2 version test. The thread does not establish that this test installation was retained, so it is modeled as a version-check measurement without a persistent system-state change.

question_patterns: Can you provide a self-contained example without the proprietary APIs?
Can you reduce this to a queued callback with an artificial delay and report how long a delay triggers the Error?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I reduced it to a queued chatbot generator. With time.sleep(5) before it starts yielding, Gradio gives an Error on the front end.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The minimal queued generator works even after waiting 30 seconds before yielding, so delay alone does not reproduce the Error.
The Error starts with a seven-second wait instead of exactly five seconds.

question_patterns: What happens in the same minimal example if you remove the artificial delay?
Does the queued generator work when it begins yielding immediately?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: If I remove the time.sleep(5) line, it works fine.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It still shows the same Error when the callback begins yielding immediately.

edges.comment: Reporter c7 after maintainers c0/c4/c6 requested a self-contained reproduction. The reduced example used Gradio 3.40.0, gradio_client 0.4.0, and Python 3.9.6; those versions enter as target-node volunteered information.

solution.intent: Treat the failure as something specific to the reporter's local environment because the same example works for the maintainer locally and in Colab.
solution.concrete_example: The example works locally and in Colab, so investigate something specific to your machine or environment.

edges.comment: Maintainer c8 suggested a local-environment cause after being unable to reproduce. Reporter c9 rejected that dismissal with the same result on their machine, a teammate's machine, and a VM, then c10 independently reported tracing the five-second failure to httpx's default timeout. These messages concern the opening reporter's own reproducer.

solution.intent: Increase the httpx timeout used by the Gradio request path so queued callbacks that take more than five seconds can return instead of producing a front-end Error, then rerun the delayed reproducer to verify it.
solution.concrete_example: As the reporter's immediate workaround, change httpx's DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_CONFIG from Timeout(timeout=5.0) to Timeout(timeout=30.0), restart the application, and rerun the queued example with the five- or seven-second delay. A proper Gradio-side fix should configure a longer timeout without requiring users to edit site-packages.

edges.comment: Reporter c10-c15 identified httpx's default five-second timeout, stated that manually setting DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_CONFIG to 30 seconds made the example work, and supplied a delayed reproducer. Gradio's maintainer agreed that timeout configuration should potentially be handled within Gradio. Later comments from other deployments, including the unrelated analytics traceback in c20-c21, are deliberately not spliced into the opening reporter's causal chain.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted cause as the httpx five-second default timeout affecting the queued Gradio request path when the callback takes longer than that before returning or yielding.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the timing evidence: the minimal queued generator fails with a five-second delay, works without the delay, and upgrading Gradio did not remove the behavior.
Must not dismiss the problem as unique to one local machine, because the reporter reproduced it on their machine, a teammate's machine, and a VM.

Must recommend increasing the applicable httpx timeout above the callback duration; editing DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_CONFIG to 30 seconds is the reporter's confirmed workaround, while configuring the timeout from Gradio is the preferred product-level direction.
Must ask the reporter to rerun the delayed queued reproducer and must not declare resolution until the front end returns normally without the Error.

persona_hint.experience_level: Moderately technical Python application developer who can reduce a LangChain chatbot to a self-contained Gradio reproducer, test multiple environments, inspect dependency source, and edit a virtual environment package configuration.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and code-heavy; supplies full examples and package versions, reports exact timing boundaries, and pushes back on environment-specific explanations with cross-machine evidence.
